This is first bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C for grant of anticipatory bail in connection with crime no.841/2022, registered at P.S - Tejaji Naar, District - Indore (M.P) for offences punishable under Sections 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC.
As per the prosecution case the applicant was working as a Hindi teacher in Kautilya Academy.
He used to assist the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage.
It is alleged that she was physically exploited by the applicant thereafter he refused to marry the prosecutrix.

A marriage card was Kapil Shrivastava vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178445820/
1 published in which the name of the girl was differently mentioned.

sentences.text: He also married some other women.
Counsel for the applicant submits that the prosecutrix is a major woman and she was a consenting party.
Further he had no intention to physically exploit the prosecutrix.
He had returned the amount whatever was deposited in his account by the family of the prosecutrix.

In support of his submission he has relied on an order passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Ansaar Mohammad Vs. The State of Rajasthan and ANR. reported in 2022 Live Law (SC) 599 wherein it has been held that where the complainant was in relationship with accused for a period of 4 years and she was a major,
the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Ansaar Mohammad Vs. The State of Rajasthan and ANR. reported in 2022 Live Law (SC) 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the State and the objector opposes the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail and submits that on perusal of the marriage card, it is apparent that the description of the prosecutrix was totally different.
Further the applicant had no intention to marry the prosecutrix.
He married another woman on the same date .
Counsel for the complainant further submits that the applicant is threatening her to withdraw the case etc.
In this regard he has made a complaint to the Police.

After hearing learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the case, I find that the applicant being a teacher was in a position to influence the student/prosecutrix and made a promise of marriage and thereafter physically exploited her.
The order relied on by the counsel for the applicant would not apply to the facts of the present case.
In view of the aforesaid, the application for grant of anticipatory bail is rejected.
Accordingly, the application is disposed off.
